Each segment re-counted directly from its rule

segments.name: High-Value Customers
segments.rule: Monthly charges ≥ $89.85 (top quartile of the dataset)

segments.name: Price-Sensitive Customers
segments.rule: Monthly charges above the median ($70.35), month-to-month contract and ≤ 1 protective add-on

segments.name: High-Churn-Risk Customers
segments.rule: Still active (Churn = No) and risk score ≥ 70% (High risk category)

segments.name: Recently Churned Customers
segments.rule: Churn = Yes (left within the dataset’s observation month)

definitions.formula: Σ MonthlyCharges of customers with Churn = No
Σ MonthlyCharges of customers with Churn = Yes — revenue already lost in the observation month
Σ MonthlyCharges of active customers in the High risk category (score ≥ 70%) — potential future exposure, not a loss yet
Σ (risk score × MonthlyCharges) over active customers — probability-weighted estimate
ARPU × restricted mean survival time (Kaplan–Meier, months)
Σ TotalCharges — cumulative billing to date, not a monthly history

cohorts.methodology: Groups are built from tenure (months since sign-up at the snapshot date) and survival is estimated with Kaplan–Meier, treating churn as the event and active customers as censored.
cohorts.limitation: The IBM Telco dataset is a single snapshot: it has no acquisition dates, churn dates or monthly status history. These are tenure bands, not true time-based acquisition cohorts, and no month-by-month retention history is shown. True cohorts would need each customer’s sign-up date, churn date and monthly active/churned snapshots.

insights.title: Contract length is the strongest churn signal
insights.detail: Month-to-month customers churn at 42.7% versus 2.8% on two-year contracts — 15.1× higher. They represent 55.0% of customers.

insights.title: Churn is concentrated early in the lifecycle
insights.detail: Customers in their first 6 months churn at 52.9%, falling to 6.6% for customers with 61–72 mo of tenure. Average tenure of churned customers is 18.0 months versus 37.6 for retained.

insights.title: Electronic check customers churn most
insights.detail: Electronic check has a 45.3% churn rate, compared with 15.2% for Credit card (automatic).

insights.title: Protective add-ons are associated with retention
insights.detail: Internet customers without tech support churn at 41.6% versus 15.2% with it. This is an association — customers who buy add-ons may differ in other ways.

insights.title: Revenue exposure
insights.detail: Churned customers represented $139,131 in monthly recurring revenue (30.5% of total MRR). A further $46,669 MRR sits with active customers classified as high risk.

insights.title: Strongest categorical association: Contract type
insights.detail: Chi-square test shows a statistically significant association with churn (Cramér’s V = 0.41). Highest churn: Month-to-month (42.7%).

recommendations.title: Convert month-to-month customers to longer contracts
recommendations.problem: Customers without a contract commitment leave at a far higher rate.
recommendations.finding: Month-to-month churn is 42.7% vs 6.8% for one- and two-year contracts.
recommendations.action: Offer tiered discounts or bundled add-ons for upgrading to a 12-month contract, timed before the 3rd and 6th billing cycles.
recommendations.impact: Scenario: a 10% relative reduction in this group's churn rate would protect ≈ $5,828 MRR per month (illustrative assumption, not a forecast).

recommendations.title: Bundle online security into internet plans
recommendations.problem: Customers without online security show elevated churn.
recommendations.finding: Churn is 41.8% without online security vs 14.6% with it.
recommendations.segment: Internet customers without online security (2,037 active)
recommendations.action: Include online security in mid-tier bundles and highlight its value at onboarding and renewal.
recommendations.impact: Scenario: a 10% relative reduction in this group's churn rate would protect ≈ $6,349 MRR per month (illustrative assumption, not a forecast).

recommendations.title: Improve technical support reach for internet customers
recommendations.problem: Internet customers without tech support churn more often.
recommendations.finding: Churn is 41.6% without tech support vs 15.2% with it (association, not proven causation).
recommendations.segment: Internet customers without tech support (2,027 active)
recommendations.action: Pilot a free 3-month tech support trial with a randomised control group to measure the true retention effect.
recommendations.impact: Scenario: a 10% relative reduction in this group's churn rate would protect ≈ $6,176 MRR per month (illustrative assumption, not a forecast).

recommendations.title: Move electronic-check payers to automatic payment
recommendations.problem: Manual payment methods are associated with higher churn.
recommendations.finding: Electronic check payers churn at 45.3% vs 16.0% for automatic bank transfer / credit card.
recommendations.action: Offer a small monthly credit for enrolling in autopay and simplify the payment-method switch flow.
recommendations.impact: Scenario: a 10% relative reduction in this group's churn rate would protect ≈ $4,350 MRR per month (illustrative assumption, not a forecast).

recommendations.title: Launch a loyalty programme for high-value customers
recommendations.problem: A small share of customers generates a large share of recurring revenue.
recommendations.finding: High-value customers (≥ $90/month) generate 38.1% of active MRR and churn at 32.7% (overall 26.5%).
recommendations.action: Create tiered loyalty rewards, priority support and annual renewal perks; assign customer-success ownership for the top accounts.
recommendations.impact: Scenario: a 10% relative reduction in this group's churn rate would protect ≈ $3,958 MRR per month (illustrative assumption, not a forecast).

recommendations.title: Investigate the fiber optic experience and price point
recommendations.problem: The premium internet product has the highest churn.
recommendations.finding: Fiber optic customers churn at 41.9% vs 19.0% for DSL, despite paying more per month.
recommendations.action: Run exit-survey and network-quality analysis for fiber users; test price-match or speed-tier right-sizing offers.
recommendations.impact: Scenario: a 10% relative reduction in this group's churn rate would protect ≈ $7,079 MRR per month (illustrative assumption, not a forecast).

recommendations.title: Strengthen the first-year customer experience
recommendations.problem: A disproportionate share of churn happens in the first 12 months.
recommendations.finding: Customers with ≤ 12 months tenure churn at 47.4% vs 17.1% after their first year.
recommendations.action: Launch a structured onboarding journey: welcome call, 30/60/90-day check-ins, proactive usage tips and an early-tenure loyalty credit.
recommendations.impact: Scenario: a 10% relative reduction in this group's churn rate would protect ≈ $2,546 MRR per month (illustrative assumption, not a forecast).

recommendations.title: Address pricing concerns for high-bill, uncommitted customers
recommendations.problem: High monthly bills without a contract are associated with elevated churn.
recommendations.finding: Month-to-month customers paying ≥ $90/month churn at 52.0% vs 22.9% for all other customers.
recommendations.action: Proactively review plan fit, offer loyalty pricing for committing to a contract, and surface the value of included services on each bill.
recommendations.impact: Scenario: a 10% relative reduction in this group's churn rate would protect ≈ $2,154 MRR per month (illustrative assumption, not a forecast).

recommendations.title: Offer assisted service for senior customers
recommendations.problem: Senior citizens churn at a higher rate.
recommendations.finding: Senior customers churn at 41.7% vs 23.6% for non-senior customers.
recommendations.action: Provide a dedicated assisted-support line and simplified plan options; review whether senior customers are over-indexed on manual payment.
recommendations.impact: Scenario: a 10% relative reduction in this group's churn rate would protect ≈ $2,198 MRR per month (illustrative assumption, not a forecast).

missingByColumn.treatment: 11 with tenure 0 set to $0 (not yet billed)

steps.title: Load dataset
steps.detail: Parsed 7,043 records and 21 attributes from "IBM Telco Customer Churn".

steps.title: Remove duplicates
steps.detail: No duplicate rows or customer IDs found.

steps.title: Convert data types
steps.detail: TotalCharges cast from text to float; SeniorCitizen (0/1) and Yes/No flags cast to boolean; tenure cast to integer; service attributes stored as categories.

steps.title: Treat missing values
steps.detail: TotalCharges: 11 blank value(s) for customers with tenure 0 set to $0. 0 blank categorical value(s) filled with "Unknown". 0 record(s) with invalid tenure, charges or churn label dropped.

steps.title: Prepare churn label
steps.detail: Churn mapped Yes → 1 (churned within the observation month) and No → 0 (retained).

steps.title: Engineer features
steps.detail: Derived tenure groups, monthly and total charge bands, count of protective add-ons (security, backup, device protection, tech support) and total subscribed services.
